claims.statement: OpenHands CodeActAgent v1.8, 0-shot and without SWE-Bench's optional hint text, resolved 26.0% of SWE-Bench Lite instances with claude-3-5-sonnet@20240620, 22.0% with gpt-4o-2024-05-13, and 7.0% with gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18.
confidence_reasons: hard, machine-tabulated result, corroborated by the authors' own prose for the claude-3.5-sonnet configuration

claims.statement: OpenHands' best SWE-Bench Lite result (26.0%) falls within the range spanned by reproducible open baselines evaluated the same way (18.0-27.3%), rather than leading or trailing that range by a wide margin.

scope.conditions: 300 instances, 0-shot, no hint text; comparison set = SWE-Agent, AutoCodeRover, Aider, Moatless Tools, Agentless

backbone LLMs differ across the compared systems (L002)

claims.statement: 0-shot, OpenHands CodeActAgent v1.5 fixed 79.3% of HumanEvalFix Python bugs with gpt-4o-2024-05-13, above every non-agentic code-LM baseline shown (16.6-48.6%), but below a 1-shot SWE-Agent baseline (87.7%) that was given a full demonstration trajectory.
confidence_reasons: hard result, corroborated by the authors' own prose
0-shot vs. 1-shot protocol difference against the strongest comparator is explicit in the claim's own scope

claims.statement: On WebArena, OpenHands' best configuration (BrowsingAgent v1.0 with claude-3.5-sonnet, 15.5%) is below two of the four specialized/trained web-agent baselines shown (AutoWebGLM 18.2%; Auto Eval & Refine 20.2%) and above the other two (Lemur 5.3%; Patel et al. 9.4%) and above a zero-shot WebArena Agent baseline (6.2-14.4%).

On MiniWoB++, OpenHands' best result (BrowsingAgent v1.0 with gpt-4o, 40.8%) exceeds one specialist baseline (Workflow Guided Exploration, 34.6%) but trails another, CC-NET, a reinforcement-learning-trained specialist (91.1%), by a wide margin.

On GPQA (diamond set), OpenHands CodeActAgent v1.8 with claude-3.5-sonnet reached 52.0% accuracy, above both few-shot chain-of-thought LLM baselines shown (29.6%, 38.8%) and above non-expert humans (21.9%), but below expert humans (81.3%).
On GAIA (L1 validation set), OpenHands GPTSwarm v1.0 reached 32.1% with gpt-4o-2024-05-13 and 30.2% with gpt-4-0125-preview, both above the AutoGPT baseline (13.2%).

On AgentBench's OS subset, OpenHands CodeActAgent v1.5 reached 57.6% with gpt-4o-2024-05-13, above the AgentBench baseline agent at both model sizes shown (42.4%, 32.6%), while OpenHands' own gpt-3.5-turbo-0125 configuration reached only 11.8%.
On the MINT math subset, OpenHands CodeActAgent v1.5 reached 77.3% with gpt-4o-2024-05-13, above the MINT baseline agent (65.8%).
On the MINT code subset, OpenHands CodeActAgent v1.5's best configuration (gpt-4o-2024-05-13, 50.0%) scored below the MINT baseline agent (gpt-4-0613, 59.6%).

On ProofWriter (5-hop subset), OpenHands CodeActAgent v1.5 reached 78.8% with gpt-4o-2024-05-13, close to but below a symbolic-solver-augmented baseline (Logic-LM, 79.6%) and above a few-shot chain-of-thought baseline (68.1%).

On Entity Deduction Arena, OpenHands CodeActAgent v1.5's best configuration (gpt-4o-2024-05-13, 38.0%) scored below a zero-shot-prompting gpt-4-0314 baseline (40.0%), while its gpt-3.5-turbo configuration (24.0%) scored below the corresponding zero-shot gpt-3.5-turbo baseline (27.0%).

On ToolQA (easy subset), OpenHands CodeActAgent v1.5 with gpt-4o-2024-05-13 reached 47.2%, the highest value in the table, while the same agent with gpt-3.5-turbo-0125 reached only 2.3%, far below the ReAct 0-shot baseline using a comparable-tier backbone (gpt-3.5-turbo, 36.8%).
confidence_reasons: the two OpenHands configurations disagree sharply, which is itself informative about backbone sensitivity

claims.statement: The authors identify five directions for future work: richer multi-modality support, stronger agents via training and inference-time techniques, better long-file editing, browsing improvements (integrating a Reflexion-based retry strategy), and automatic workflow generation.
confidence_reasons: claim type 'future' names a direction rather than an empirical assertion; 'confidence' is not a natural fit for this type and is set conservatively

limitations.statement: No seed count, repeated-run, standard deviation, or confidence interval is reported for any success-rate number across the 15 benchmarks, for either OpenHands agents or baselines.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: Every numeric margin in this paper, including the cross-category generality finding, should be read as a single-run point estimate rather than a statistically characterized effect.
limitations.resolution: Would require the original authors to re-run key comparisons with multiple seeds and report spread.

limitations.statement: Cross-agent comparisons vary the backbone LLM (e.g. gpt-4o-mini, gpt-4o, claude-3.5-sonnet, gpt-3.5-turbo variants for OpenHands; a different, sometimes older or smaller, model for each baseline) rather than holding it fixed.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: Differences between OpenHands and baseline agents may partly reflect backbone model capability rather than platform or agent design; the generality finding cannot be attributed to the platform alone from this evidence.
limitations.resolution: Would require re-running the platform and baselines on a matched set of backbone models.

limitations.statement: OpenHands is not the top performer in the comparison set on several individual benchmarks: WebArena (below AutoWebGLM and Auto Eval & Refine), MiniWoB++ (well below CC-NET), HumanEvalFix (below a 1-shot SWE-Agent baseline), the MINT code subset (below the MINT baseline agent), Entity Deduction Arena (below a zero-shot baseline at both model sizes compared), and ToolQA with one specific backbone (gpt-3.5-turbo-0125).
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: The cross-category claim is about simultaneous breadth of competence, not about leading every benchmark; presenting it as anything stronger than 'competitive but rarely best' would overclaim.
limitations.resolution: Would require targeted improvements to the specific agents/skills underperforming on these benchmarks.

limitations.statement: Benchmark subsets (SWE-Bench 'Lite', ML-Bench 'quarter subset', ToolQA 'easy subset', GPQA 'diamond' set), the exclusion of SWE-Bench's optional hint text, and baseline numbers drawn from cited original papers rather than re-run by the authors under identical conditions all vary across rows in ways that limit direct comparability.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: Some of the numeric gaps between OpenHands and baselines may partly reflect differing evaluation conditions rather than agent capability alone.
limitations.resolution: Would require re-running all systems under one held-fixed protocol.

limitations.statement: The architecture and version numbers evaluated (CodeActAgent v1.5/v1.8, BrowsingAgent v1.0, GPTSwarm v1.0) describe a specific, dated snapshot (evaluated circa mid-to-late 2024). Later project material describes a substantially restructured system: a separate 'software-agent-sdk', a 'V1' runtime, and an 'Agent Canvas' front end, with a concrete SDK change dated November 17, 2025.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: Implementation-level details in this paper's Platform section should not be assumed to describe the currently shipping system; the evaluation's evidentiary value is about the design principles (general action space, sandboxing, ACI, delegation) rather than about any specific current build.
limitations.resolution: Would require a fresh evaluation of the current system for currency.

limitations.statement: No experiment in the paper varies one architectural component (event-stream design, sandboxed action space, the AgentSkills/ACI library, multi-agent delegation) while holding the others and the backbone LLM fixed.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: The paper's evidence supports that the *system as a whole* is competitive across categories; it does not isolate which component of the platform is responsible, so mechanistic explanations of *why* are speculative.
limitations.resolution: Would require targeted ablations of each platform component under matched conditions.

limitations.statement: The risk-mitigation properties claimed for OpenHands (C020) are asserted in an ethics statement, not measured by any safety-specific benchmark among the 15 evaluated; a dedicated safety benchmark appears only in later project material, after publication.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: The paper's safety/impact framing should be read as a stated intention and design rationale, not as an empirically demonstrated safety property.
limitations.resolution: Would require an empirical safety evaluation, e.g. on a dedicated agent-safety benchmark.
